home.alt: A marble bust of Aristotle, head in profile to the right, on a round stand.
home.what: Aristoteles. Apud Fulvium Ursinum in marmore
home.where: © The Trustees of the British Museum

Cat.alt: A ladder of ringed words set in the crown of a leafy tree: Ens, Substantia, Corpus, Vivens, Animal, Homo down the trunk to Petrus Paulus, with the differences in subsistens, corpoream, animatum, sensitivum, rationale on the left and their opposites on the right, joined by bands lettered Dividitur, Constituit and Repugnat.
Cat.who: Edme Pourchot (Purchotius), author; engraved by Fillœul ('Fillœul Sculp.' on the plate)
Cat.what: 'Arbor Porphyrii secundum doctrinam Aristotelis et Peripateticorum', Tab. 1, plate in Institutiones philosophicae ad faciliorem veterum et recentiorum philosophorum intelligentiam comparatae, fourth edition
Cat.how: Engraving (the Deutsche Digitale Bibliothek record lists '33 Ill. (Kupferst.)'; the plate is signed 'Filloeul Sculp.')
Cat.where: Staatsbibliothek Bamberg (Ph.q.88), digitised by the Bayerische Staatsbibliothek
Cat.lic: No Copyright – Non-Commercial Use Only (rightsstatements.org NoC-NC 1.0, as the holder's manifest states)

Int.alt: Four boxed statements about a man running at the corners of a square, joined by bands marked Contrariae, Subalternae and Subcontrariae and crossed by two bands of Contradictoriae.
Int.who: Bernardo Sannig (author, as the holder gives it)
Int.what: Fig. I, square of opposition (Omnis homo currit, Nullus homo currit, Quidam homo currit, Quidam homo non currit; Contraria, Subalterna, Contradictoria, Subcontraria), in Schola philosophica scotistarum, seu Cursus philosophicus completus, ad mentem doctoris subtilis Joannis Duns Scoti, authore P.F. Bernardo Sannig, tomus 1 (the printed label 'Fig: I' and a foxing spot are blotted from the cut)
Int.how: Printed figure (the holder does not name the process)
Int.where: Staatsbibliothek Bamberg (Ph.f.39#1), via the Bavarian State Library's digital collections
Int.lic: No Copyright – Non-Commercial Use Only (NoC-NC 1.0), as the holder gives it

Isa.alt: A tree of linked circles, Substantia, Corpus, Vivens and Animal down the middle, with paired circles on each side joined by bands marked Dividitur, Constituit and Repugnat
Isa.what: Arbor Porphyrii, from Institutiones philosophicae, volume 1

APr.alt: Rows of overlapping circles lettered A, B and C, some marked with a star, numbered Fig. 1 to Fig. 22.
APr.who: Leonhard Euler; translated by Henry Hunter (engraver not named)
APr.what: Plate II, Second Series, in Letters of Euler on different subjects in physics and philosophy, volume 1
APr.where: Boston Public Library, via the Internet Archive

APo.alt: Dense lines of Greek in abbreviated type giving the proof, ending in a small circle with a diameter and chords from a point on the rim, labelled with Greek letters.
APo.who: Euclid; edited by Simon Grynaeus (Basel edition, with Proclus on Book I)
APo.what: Elements Book III, Prop. 31 (λα), proof and figure, p. 42 (folio), in Ευκλείδου Στοιχείων βιβλ. ιε′ (Greek only)
APo.how: Printed type and figure (the holder does not name the process)
APo.where: National Central Library of Rome, via the Internet Archive (Google Books scan)
APo.lic: Public Domain Mark (the Internet Archive record states the Creative Commons Public Domain Mark 1.0)

Top.alt: Three men in wigs and gowns stand together in a columned room, two of them gesturing at each other and the third reading from a book.
Top.who: Unidentified engraver signing GWHWHNM; sold by John Bowles
Top.what: The Triple Plea (law, physic and divinity dispute which ranks highest)
Top.credit: Personifications of law, medicine and theology argue over the superiority of their respective professions. Engraving by GWHWHNM, ca. 1720. Wellcome Collection. Public Domain Mark. Source: Wellcome Collection.

SE.alt: Six men in caps and gowns sit and stand round a draped table, bent over an open book, one old man talking and pointing.
SE.who: Hans Burgkmair (I), named on the object
SE.what: Zes geleerden zitten rond een tafel (Six scholars sit round a table over a book), block first used in Liber theoricae nec non praticae Alsaharavii
SE.when: Augsburg, 1519 (block first used; the Rijksmuseum dates the print 1483-1519)
SE.lic: Public Domain Mark 1.0 (the Rijksmuseum also lists CC0)

Phys.alt: Concentric rings with lettering: earth, water, air and fire at the centre, then the seven planetary spheres, the fixed stars, the Primum Mobile, the Crystalline sphere and the Empyrean.
Phys.who: Peter Apian and Gemma Frisius (author and editor), printer Joannes Withagius
Phys.what: Schema praedictae divisionis (diagram of the elemental region and the heavenly spheres, Empyreum at the rim), page 6 of the first part of Cosmographia, siue descriptio vniuersi orbis
Phys.how: Printed figure (the holder does not name the process)
Phys.where: John Carter Brown Library, via the Internet Archive

Cael.alt: An armillary sphere on an ornate stand, a small earth at the centre of crossed rings and a band of zodiac signs
Cael.what: Sphère armillaire, Encyclopédie, Astronomie, plate II

GC.alt: A round wheel with eight discs (four elements and four qualities) joined by bands marked Contraria, Conuenientes and Repugnantes, with a lettered ring around a central circle.
GC.what: Figura elementarium primariumque qualitatum, tam conuenientium quam discordantium inuicem (wheel of the elements Ignis, Aer, Aqua, Terra and the qualities hot, cold, wet, dry), page 2 of Book I of Sphaera mundi
GC.how: Printed figure (the holder does not name the process)
GC.where: John Carter Brown Library, via the Internet Archive

Mete.alt: A great comet streams across a starry sky above dark fields and a river
Mete.credit: Astronomy: a comet in the night sky. Wood engraving, ca. 1860. Wellcome Collection. Public Domain Mark. Source: Wellcome Collection.

DA.alt: A man's head in profile with a band across the skull divided into cells with Latin labels, lines running from the eye, nose, ear and mouth to the cells.
DA.what: Head with the inner senses (fantasia, sensus communis, imaginativa, cogitativa, aestimativa, memorativa) and the outer senses, from Margarita philosophica nova, Book X, tract 2
DA.how: Printed figure (the holder does not name the process)
DA.where: John Carter Brown Library, via the Internet Archive

Sens.alt: A single human eye, engraved large, with its lashes and brow
Sens.what: Anatomy: organs of sense, the eye, plate I
Sens.credit: The human eye: ten figures, showing the eye open and closed. Engraving by T. Milton, 1809. Wellcome Collection. Public Domain Mark. Source: Wellcome Collection.

Mem.alt: The wax impression of an engraved gem: a young ruler’s head in profile, with a headband and a cloak of scales
Mem.what: A Descriptive Catalogue of Ancient and Modern Engraved Gems, cast by James Tassie, plate LV
Mem.where: Boston Public Library, via the Internet Archive

Somn.alt: A child asleep, its head of curls turned on the pillow, eyes closed
Somn.where: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York

Insomn.alt: A man slumped asleep over a desk with owls, bats and a cat crowding behind him.
Insomn.what: Plate 43 from Los Caprichos: The sleep of reason produces monsters (El sueño de la razon produce monstruos)
Insomn.where: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York

DivSomn.alt: A woman asleep in a canopied bed; above her, in a cloud, a winged dragon hovers over a walled city and river.
DivSomn.who: Anonymous printmaker, after a design by Jörg Breu the Younger; publisher Heinrich Steiner (as the Rijksmuseum gives it)
DivSomn.what: Droom van Skanderbegs moeder (Dream of Skanderbeg's mother), illustration in Marinus Barletius, Scanderbeg

Long.alt: A very tall oak with a thick trunk in a park of old oaks, a horse standing at its foot
Long.what: The Tall Oak at Fredville, from Sylva Britannica

Juv.alt: Two front views of the lungs with the larynx and ringed windpipe above, the left with the heart's place between the lobes, the right with the lobes drawn aside from a central sac.
Juv.who: Bartolomeo Eustachi (author); the holder names no engraver
Juv.what: Tab. XV, six figures of the lungs with the larynx and trachea (figures I and IV used), in Tabulae anatomicae
Juv.how: Printed figure (the holder does not name the process)
Juv.where: Wellcome Library, via the Internet Archive
Juv.lic: Public Domain Mark (the Internet Archive record states: 'available under the Creative Commons, Public Domain Mark')

HA.alt: Eight sea animals on one sheet: an octopus, two cuttlefish, two squids, a sea hare, a small squid and a tiny cuttlefish, with a sprig of eggs.
HA.who: Johannes Jonston (author); engraver not named by the holder
HA.what: Tab. I, octopus (Polypus), cuttlefish (Sepia), squids (Loligo) and sepiola, in Historiae naturalis de exanguibus aquaticis libri IV
HA.how: Copper-plate figures (the title page says "cum figuris Æneis")
HA.where: Naturalis Biodiversity Center, via the Internet Archive

PA.alt: A horse's heart lying open among the folds of the two lungs, windpipe and great vessels above.
PA.what: The Lungs and Heart (Farriery, plate IX), dissection of a horse's lungs and heart
PA.how: Engraving with etching, coloured by hand
PA.credit: Dissection of a horse's lungs and heart: three figures. Coloured engraving by J. Pass after Harguinier, 1805. Wellcome Collection. Public Domain Mark. Source: Wellcome Collection.

IA.alt: The skeleton of a horse stepping forward with one foreleg raised, and a human skeleton striding beside it
IA.what: Skeleton of a man, with the skeleton of a horse, in action, plate V of A Comparative View of the Human and Animal Frame
IA.credit: Skeleton of a man, with the skeleton of a horse, in action. Lithograph by B. Waterhouse Hawkins, 1860. Wellcome Collection. Public Domain Mark. Source: Wellcome Collection.

MA.alt: A flayed male figure in a deep lunge, one arm swung back and one thrust forward, his muscles, ribs and hip bone drawn
MA.what: Plate 10 of Anatomie du gladiateur combattant
MA.where: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York

GA.alt: A child at term with hands and feet drawn up, in the opened womb, the cord and membranes beside it.
GA.who: William Hunter (author); drawn by J. van Rymsdyk, engraved by R. Strange (plate signed "delin." and "sculp.")
GA.what: Tab. XII (child at term in the opened uterus, seen from behind), in Anatomia uteri humani gravidi tabulis illustrata
GA.where: Wellcome Library, via the Internet Archive
GA.lic: Public Domain Mark (the Internet Archive record states: 'available under the Creative Commons, Public Domain Mark')

Meta.alt: Plato pointing upward and Aristotle with his palm held level walk side by side down the steps of a vaulted hall, other philosophers around them
Meta.where: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
Meta.credit: Gift of Lucy Chauncey, in memory of her father, Henry Chauncey, 1935

EN.alt: A long Doric temple of heavy fluted columns, with trees on the entablature and three men and a horse in front.
EN.what: View showing the remains of a large enclosure of columns, from Différentes vues de quelques Restes de trois grands Edifices ... de Pesto autrement Posidonia
EN.where: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
EN.lic: CC0 (Open Access; The Met lists the object as public domain)
EN.credit: Gift of Mrs. Carroll G. Ross, 1945

EE.alt: A woman balancing a sieve on her head stands on a ladder among people tending a sick man, gathering firewood, storing food and mending a house.
EE.who: Philips Galle, after Pieter Bruegel the Elder; published by Hieronymus Cock
EE.where: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York

Pol.alt: Solon sits writing on a tablet beside a column while two men, a helmeted soldier and three veiled women stand watching.
Pol.what: Solon writing laws for Athens, from Merry's Museum
Pol.how: Print (the volume does not name its technique)
Pol.where: Prelinger Library, via the Internet Archive

Oec.alt: An old farmhouse with an outside stair: a woman on the stair scatters feed to ducks below, another sits by the door with a baby, and small children play in the yard
Oec.where: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
Oec.credit: Gift of William Loring Andrews, 1883, transferred from the Library

VV.alt: A seated woman counts coins at a table under a ruined roof, around her hooded and fishlike figures hoard, steal and crawl among coins, bags and burning ruins.
VV.who: Pieter van der Heyden, after Pieter Bruegel the Elder; published by Hieronymus Cock
VV.where: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York

DM.alt: A globe at the centre of nested rings for the planets and a tilted band of zodiac signs inside a ring of latitude lines.
DM.who: Andreas Cellarius, engraved by Jan van Loon
DM.what: Scenographia systematis mundani Ptolemaici, plate 2 of Harmonia macrocosmica
DM.how: Engraving, coloured by hand (cut as black ink)
DM.where: National Library of Australia (Rex Nan Kivell Collection, Map NK 10241)

Mech.alt: A spoked wheel with a cord and a 6 lb weight on the axle and a 1 lb weight on the rim.
Mech.what: Wheel and axle (figure 10 of five), Principles of science, Large series, No. 2, Mechanical powers
Mech.where: David Rumsey Map Collection, David Rumsey Map Center, Stanford Libraries, via the Internet Archive
Mech.credit: David Rumsey Map Collection, David Rumsey Map Center, Stanford Libraries

Col.alt: Two concentric rainbows over a flat country of farm buildings and trees under a cloudy sky, small letters along the horizon.
Col.what: Meteorology: a double rainbow over fields in the country
Col.credit: Meteorology: a double rainbow over fields in the country. Engraving by Royce, 1805. Wellcome Collection. Public Domain Mark. Source: Wellcome Collection.

Phgn.alt: A lion’s head seen from the front beside a bearded man’s head seen from the front, the brow and hair drawn alike
Phgn.who: L. P. Baltard and A. Le Grand, after Charles Le Brun
Phgn.what: Dissertation sur un traité de Charles Le Brun, concernant le rapport de la physionomie humaine avec celle des animaux
Phgn.where: Wellcome Library, via the Internet Archive

MXG.alt: A round figure of concentric bands, a cloud ring, a dark ring, ringed bands and a sun with a face at the centre.
MXG.who: Robert Fludd; plates engraved by Johann Theodor de Bry and Matthäus Merian the elder
MXG.what: Concentric rings of cloud and light around a sun, from Utriusque cosmi historia, volume 1
MXG.where: Getty Research Institute, via the Internet Archive

Aud.alt: A head in profile, cut open to show the outer ear, the passage and drum, the small bones and the inner ear, with a probe in the ear
Aud.what: An External and Internal View of the Organ of Hearing in Situ, from An Engraved Representation of the Anatomy of the Human Ear
Aud.credit: An engraved representation of the anatomy of the human ear. To which are added surgical remarks ... and a synoptic table of the diseases of the ear. Exhibiting in one view the external and internal parts of that organ in situ / [Thomas Buchanan]. Public Domain Mark. Source: Wellcome Collection.

Lin.alt: Ancient bronze compasses and calipers above a long folding rule, shown open and half folded
Lin.note: Bronze compasses, calipers and a folding foot-rule found at Pompeii. Dots on the rule mark sixteen digits on one face and twelve inches on the other.
Lin.what: Real Museo Borbonico, volume VI, plate XV: bronze measures from Pompeii
Lin.where: Wellcome Library, via the Internet Archive

Vent.alt: A circle of twenty-four wind names in Latin set round a ring with a star-shaped diagram of lines inside.
Vent.who: Attributed to Peter Flötner and others, for Walther Ryff’s Vitruvius
Vent.what: Figur der vier und zwentzig Wind, p. 96 of Vitruuius ... zehen Buecher von der Architectur
Vent.where: Getty Research Institute, via the Internet Archive

Mirab.alt: A horse with a long straight horn on its brow leaps over open ground.
Mirab.what: Monoceros Unicornu Einhorn, upper figure of Tab. X, in Historiae naturalis de quadrupedibus libri
Mirab.when: apud Ioannem Iacobi fil. Schipper, 1657 (place not given in the holder's record)
Mirab.how: Copperplate figures (the title states "cum aeneis figuris")
Mirab.where: National Library of Naples, via the Internet Archive

Rhet.alt: A stout man in an eighteenth-century coat stands on a step with one arm stretched out and speaks to a crowded hall of deputies while a priest and others in the foreground look up at him.
Rhet.who: Anonymous (draughtsman-lithographer); printed by Veuve Gosselin, Paris
Rhet.what: Mirabeau à l'Assemblée des États Généraux (Carnavalet inventory G.27667BIS)
Rhet.where: Musée Carnavalet, Histoire de Paris (Paris Musées)

Poet.alt: Four mourning figures in long robes, three carrying jars, walk in a row with heads bowed.
Poet.what: Orestes, Electra and the Chorus of Trojan Dames bring oblations (Choephorae 1), plate 19 of Compositions from the Tragedies of Aeschylus
Poet.where: Internet Archive (scan from microfilm, Eighteenth Century Collections)

MM.alt: Two engraved heads side by side: at left a head in a headcloth with raised brows and wide eyes, at right a young man with long curls and a calm, level gaze.
MM.who: Charles Le Brun, engraved by John Tinney
MM.what: Desire, and Joy with Tranquility, plate 4 of a set of Le Brun’s passions
MM.credit: A woman's face expressing desire (left) and a man's face expressing 'joy with tranquility' (right). Engraving, c. 1760, after C. Le Brun. Wellcome Collection. Public Domain Mark. Source: Wellcome Collection.

Prob.alt: In a study with jars, a hung crocodile and drawers of papers, an old man in a fur-edged coat sights a long telescope through a window of stars while a young man holds a book.
Prob.who: Charles Grignion the Elder, after Samuel Wale, as the holder gives it (the plate is signed I. Taylor)
Prob.what: Astronomy: an astronomer in his study, looking out of the window with a telescope
Prob.when: Not dated by the holder (Wale, the designer, died in 1786)
Prob.how: Print (the holder gives both engraving and woodcut)
Prob.credit: Astronomy: an astronomer in his study, looking out of the window with a telescope. Engraving by C. Grignion after S. Wale. Wellcome Collection. Public Domain Mark. Source: Wellcome Collection.

Plant.alt: One strawberry plant shown whole, with its fibrous roots, a crown of stalks, large toothed leaves, flowers and ripe fruit.
Plant.what: Fraga fructu magno, with the white and red strawberries, Hortus Eystettensis
Plant.where: Wellcome Library, via the Internet Archive

Spir.alt: Both lungs seen from behind, each in an upper and a lower lobe, with the windpipe's branches and the great vessels running between them, in shaded engraving.
Spir.who: Benoît-Louis Prévost, after Albrecht von Haller
Spir.what: Anatomie, second plate XVI, figure 2: the lungs and their vessels, Encyclopédie
Spir.credit: The arteries and lungs (fig. 2), after Haller; the breast (fig. 3), after Nuck; branch of the bronchi (fig. 4), after Bidloo. Engraving by Prevost, 1762. Wellcome Collection. Public Domain Mark. Source: Wellcome Collection.

RhetAl.alt: A bearded old man in a hooded cloak holds a scroll while a curly-haired child sits on a cushioned chair with a hand at his brow; fluted columns stand behind them.
RhetAl.who: Johann Sebastian Müller (?), after Johann Heinrich Ramberg
RhetAl.lic: © The Trustees of the British Museum, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0
RhetAl.credit: Donated by: Hon Christopher Lennox-Boyd (executors of)

AthPol.alt: A long Doric temple seen from a corner, with fourteen columns on its flank and a pediment, standing on a rise with a ruined tower behind and a few seated and mounted men in the foreground.
AthPol.who: Julien-David Le Roy, engraved by Le Bas
AthPol.what: Vue du Temple de Thésée, plate XI of Les ruines des plus beaux monuments de la Grèce
AthPol.where: Getty Research Institute, via the Internet Archive
